instructions: This conversation is fictional. Listen to the conversation before reading the transcript and answer independently. After submitting, check the transcript and reasons for any errors.
transcript:
Ella: The community room needs some maintenance before the book event on Saturday. I have made a short list, but I do not want anyone to start work without the manager.
Jon: Good. What did you notice first?
Ella: The kitchen faucet drips, and the drain below the sink is slow. A pipe was checked last month, but the floor is still damp near the cupboard.
Jon: My uncle calls a faucet a tap. I will ask the office to send a qualified worker to inspect both the faucet and the drain. What time can someone meet them?
Ella: The manager can meet the worker between two and three on Thursday. I will take a photo of the damp area for the report. The carpet is dry, so we can leave it where it is.
Jon: There is also a crack near the roof window. It was noticed on Tuesday, and the office has already contacted a specialist. The curtain was moved away from it.
Ella: The cupboard handle is loose too. A carpenter will decide whether to tighten the screw or replace the hinge. I found an old bolt in the drawer, but we should not assume it fits.
Jon: The carpenter brought a hammer, a nail and a drill to mend a wooden frame last time. This job may need different equipment. We will let the worker choose how to fix it.
Ella: What about the light? The bulb was replaced in March, but it is not working today. There is a cable near the socket, and I can see a wire beside the switch.
Jon: Please leave those alone. The office will ask a qualified technician to check them. The lock was checked yesterday, and the two keys are in the office.
Ella: I will send the list now. The carpenter plans to come on Friday. If the old fitting is difficult to loosen, the worker can explain the next step.
Jon: Thanks. The building manager will decide what work is needed.
